Dark and gritty fantasy that hits similar feels to dark souls, all with a lovecraft overtone. The highs over overcoming a boss/situation/dungeon vs the lows of losing that favoured party member all while your heroes battle the stresses of this grim world that change how you have to react to situations. This game perfectly combines board and video games with amazing art and sound design and I genuinely love it.

Do not assume that you will beat this game, do not assume there is a happy ending for any of your heroes when picking them from the new arrivals and do not assume that your blood will not boil (at times!). With these things in mind you are set for Darkest Dungeon.

Look no further, here's an absolute summary of all complaints about this game:

1) Early access, so not a lot of content yet.
2) RNG Gods are merciless.

And here's an absolute summary of why these complaints are stupid:

1) That's what early access is. More content will be added.
2) Check this out, because this is one of the reasons I LOVE this game: the very first page after booting the game is a disclaimer stating how "Darkest Dungeon is making the best of a bad situation".

Get it? Failing is the default outcome of this game, so you MUST learn to take small victories, one at a time, building yourself up slowly. This is why a lot of the upgrades involve lowering the cost of upgrades; so that you can pick yourself back up when things go badly.

Some dungeon runs you'll net 40k gold, and others all your level six heroes with Legendary equip will die from eight consecutive enemy critical hits.

You must do all it takes, and not give up... to survive in the shadow of the...

this game isn't hard, its just pure RNG hell garbage, its practically a dice rolling simulator with an edgy dnd skin.

good "hard" games CAN and honestly SHOULD use rng to spice up the runs, but still give the players all the tools necessary to win regardless of luck on skill alone, this game does not do that, everything is luck reliant, from the loot, to the gargabe heart attack/stress system, to the needlessly low accuracy, to the encounters, to the crit system etc.

its like someone looked at pokemon and thought "what if we got all of the bad parts of this, increased them 10 fold and put an edgy skin over it, while reducing the fun of rng variety to almost nothing", this is a study on how to not use luck in a game; when thinking of implementing randomness and "rogue" system in their games, devs should aspire to be TBOI (or even F&H for a more low budged example), NOT this.

This game is trying, difficult, and stressful. Your heroes die and stay dead. You will become acquainted with madness, and the heroes will suffer from your missteps. But, whether the rewards make up for this or the player is a masochist, perhaps both, the game is strangely enjoyable.

Hire new recruits, build up the hamlet, and prepare yourself to fight against the ravenous, clutching shadows of... the Darkest Dungeon!

There is more to adventuring than loot, glory and fortune. What Darkest Dungeon does is turn the classic heroic adventurers into marionettes used by an unseen hand to feed into the meat grinder. One way to approach the darkest dungeon is to consider it a realistic mercenary captain simulator where you send gangs of fighters on skirmishes around the area to reclaim artefacts, gain a foothold and slay the enemy leaders. During these forays the "heroes" are assailed by unspeakable horrors, horrendous injuries and soul shattering anguish in a bold quest to reclaim your ancestral home, opulent and imperial..

This game is simply magnificent in its theming with a splendid mixture of Old World Warhammer Fantasy, Victoriana and Lovecraftian horror. The artwork, the music and the environments are splendid and really sells you a bleak and foreboding atmosphere. The games narration delivered by Wayne June is the stuff of legends and completely submerges you in cosmic horror. The gameplay is a mixture of turn based combat with a resourcemanagement in the form of heroes' sanity, sickness and supplies. As with Dark Souls before it you will die, alot.. However there is a mastery to be found and once you get into the games mindset it is a rewarding puzzle to mix and match the different classes to form your ultimate theme.

There are also a ton of mods to try out should you tire on the base game!

Highly recommended to anyone into dark fantastic squad based sanitymanagers!

Darkest Dungeon is a very punishing turn-based RPG that borders on being antagonistic. There have been times I've had to take a break from the game, because I've pushed my party a little more than I should have and had characters I've invested a great deal of time on die. You are always able to run away, keeping your loot, so there really is no excuse for this.
Introducing stress (which can lead to mental breakdown or even heart attack) as well as fine grained physical damage, disease, bleeding and other physical ailments, this game is incredibly detailed. You will develop your town, learn more about your family secrets and build skills, armor and weaponry for a multitude of character classes. The dark, gothic pen and ink graphical style and throbbing music, are accompanied by a narrator.
Highly recommended, very addictive.

This game is so fucking cool.

PROS
- An incredible atmosphere.
- You'll be tense. No FNAF jump scare, no forced drama. The atmosphre combined with the way combat plays out is tense.
- Easy to learn, difficult to master turn-based strategy combat.
- Missions feel rewarding.
- The game is structured to be difficult, without being frustrating. You are punished for mistakes, but not in a way that makes the game impossible to continue. Probably the only TB Strat game I haven't been inspired to memory hack or savescum.
- Very cool narration. The monologues are very heavy, but they're written surprisingly well. They're dark and edgy, but smooth enough to enjoy. It's also not a GLaDOS or Bastion knockoff, narration is its own thing and superb.

CONS
- Narration is good, but often repeated. It's not totally repetitive, there's enough going on to not be bored of it, but I really hope they hire this guy and give him some more lines for common tasks.
- The tense edge dulls after you get an understanding of the mechanics and it becomes more strategy based, but that's obvious with any horror game.

Strong recommendation for strategy lovers. The atmosphere is oddly reminiscent of Diablo.

What drew me to the game first, was the art. It has a beautiful, rough, dark style, heavily inspired by Mike Mignola. The art style was specifically chosen to present the dark, brooding nature of a dungeon crawl that involves fighting Lovecraftian Horrors.

What kept me playing was the game play.

The game is spare, minimal, focused on the organization of a dungeop party, and then sheparding them through a gritty, dangerous labyrinth, as their minds fray, as they sicken, as they're slowly driven insane by the things they have to face.

Counter balancing this, you manage the township, building up resources and facilities to help care for and train your teams.

The game offers a wonderful, fresh look at the idea of the dungeon crawl, dealing heavily with the accumlation of psychologial problems a dungeon party would face.

Additionally, the game is turn based, and any given dungeon run can be completed in 15 to 30 minutes, making the game highly compartmentalized, and easy to play in small chunks of time. The game also allows you to save and quit anywhere.

Be warned though, Darkest Dungeon is of a "Rogue-Like" nature, it's harsh and unforgiving, and your best and brightest will die.

An excelent and innovative game, sort of a dungeon crawling with some strategy and management included. Its a refreshing and tense experience. It has a gothic/lovecraftian theme and its all about the stress resulting of surviving on a dark and menacing world, full of monstruosities and things unknown. Be prepared to pass some stress too cause RNG here is real, even if you prepare a well adjusted and strong party to the next mission, the result could be a frustrating failure. Its part of the game, sometimes you loose all or run to survive for another day. Managing your "heroes" is not an easy task and insanity is at bay. Nonetheless its very rewarding when your party get home safe, with all the treasures, even after some suffering and gaining some psychological flaws. If you like RPG, dungeon crawling, lovecraftian atmosphere and a real challenge, get this one!

No game is perfect, but this one comes very close. This game promises a difficult challenge & dark atmosphere, delivering on both flawlessly. There is no protagonist, nobody is a hero, just normal people struggling the best they can to overcome unnatural horrors, their own mortality & the fragility of their own minds. Even if you do everything right & play perfectly, a single roll of the dice will still inevitably lead to somebody's permanent end.

Replay value is extraordinarily high, with higher difficulty modes offering more mechanics, harsher penalties & new restrictions and limitations. With one of the largest workshops full of DLC that I've personally seen & mods being constantly added & updated, you have a near-limitless source of ways to make the game fresh & interesting. Furthermore, mods do NOT disable achievements, so feel free & have at it.
